title: Core-flow end-to-end adherence probe refuses ship without captured evidence every core flow completes against the shipped runtime
asA: operator relying on the journey-completeness discipline the SPA blueprint declares
iWant: a runtime check that fails the build unless every core user flow the application enumerates completes end-to-end against the shipped runtime with real providers and captured evidence, with authentication always included when the application has any authentication surface
soThat: an app is never signed off as done while its core flows (authentication first) are unproven end-to-end in the production runtime, and 'a workaround exists' explicitly does not convert a broken flow into a passing check

acceptanceCriteria.description: The application enumerates its core user flows in a stable, discoverable manifest at ship-time. Each enumerated flow names a flow id, an entry-point route, an ordered sequence of user-driven steps that reach a terminal success state, and a terminal success assertion (a DOM signal, a URL, or an authenticated-session signal). When the application declares any authentication surface (spa-REQ-009), authentication is ALWAYS enumerated as a core flow; the probe refuses ship when the manifest omits an authentication flow while spa-REQ-009 surfaces are present.
acceptanceCriteria.given: the application boot topology at ship
acceptanceCriteria.then: the manifest exists at the stable path the probe reads, enumerates every declared core flow with the required fields, and includes an authentication flow whenever the application has a spa-REQ-009 authentication surface

acceptanceCriteria.description: Every enumerated core flow executes end-to-end against the SHIPPED runtime: the same server construction the production entry point boots (same route registration, same production security-header stack, same middleware, same static-asset serving), driven by a real headless browser against real external-service providers (not stubbed adapters, not app.inject, not a bespoke test harness). The probe refuses ship when any flow ran through an in-process fetch, a mocked provider, a header-stripping harness, or a server instance the production entry point does not construct.
acceptanceCriteria.when: every enumerated core flow is executed by a real browser against the shipped construction
acceptanceCriteria.then: every flow runs through the production entry-point path with real providers; any flow executed against a mocked provider or a bypassed header path refuses ship

acceptanceCriteria.description: For every enumerated core flow the probe captures evidence sufficient to reconstruct the run: the ordered navigation trace (routes visited with response status codes), the terminal DOM assertion result, the wall-clock timing per step, and any provider-side ids the flow generated (e.g. an emailed magic-link id, a payment-provider intent id). A skipped, timed-out, or absent evidence entry for any enumerated core flow is a HARD REFUSAL; 'a documented workaround exists', a status.md quirk line, an operator note, or a mint-your-own-token bypass explicitly does NOT convert a broken or skipped flow into a passing verdict.
acceptanceCriteria.given: an enumerated core flow whose captured evidence is absent, marked 'skipped', or ends in a non-success terminal state
acceptanceCriteria.then: the flow is recorded as 'fail' (or 'skip') and the probe refuses ship; no workaround note, README caveat, or documented quirk overrides the refusal

acceptanceCriteria.description: For every core flow that fails or is skipped, the probe writes a machine-readable refusal on the report naming the flow id, the entry-point route, the step at which the flow diverged from expectation, the assertion that did not hold, and the captured evidence up to the divergence. The refusal renders in the probe's stdout with the flow id and the report path, so a ci-pipeline operator reading the runner output sees which flow refused and where to look. Silent-log refusals are not permitted; every refusal exits the probe non-zero.
acceptanceCriteria.given: any core flow the probe records as 'fail' or 'skip'
acceptanceCriteria.then: the probe report carries a structured refusal entry naming the flow, the divergence step, and the failing assertion; stdout names the flow id and the report path; the process exit is non-zero

acceptanceCriteria.description: The core-flow end-to-end probe (TAC-211) writes a JSON report at a stable relative path ('reports/core-flow-e2e-adherence.json' under the configured report directory) naming every core flow enumerated, its captured evidence entry, its per-flow verdict ('ok' | 'fail' | 'skip'), and an aggregate 'verdict' field of 'ok' | 'deployed-with-defects'. The 'ok' aggregate is reserved for runs in which every enumerated core flow lands 'ok'; any 'fail' or 'skip' entry lands the aggregate at 'deployed-with-defects'.
acceptanceCriteria.given: a completed probe run (pass or fail)
acceptanceCriteria.when: the report file is inspected on disk
acceptanceCriteria.then: the JSON at 'reports/core-flow-e2e-adherence.json' matches the shape declared by TAC-211 and its aggregate 'verdict' agrees with the process exit code (0 for 'ok', non-zero for 'deployed-with-defects')

acceptanceCriteria.description: When the core-flow end-to-end probe is wired as a gate in the ci-pipeline runner (TAC-701), a non-zero probe exit propagates through the per-gate report (TAC-702) and the aggregate report (TAC-703), and the ci-pipeline runner refuses ship with a non-zero exit. The 'deployed-with-defects' probe verdict maps deterministically to a 'failed' entry in the TAC-703 aggregate; a run cannot land the pipeline aggregate at 'passed' while any enumerated core flow ran as 'fail' or 'skip'.
acceptanceCriteria.given: the ci-pipeline runner configured with the core-flow end-to-end probe as a required gate
acceptanceCriteria.when: the probe reports 'deployed-with-defects' on any run
acceptanceCriteria.then: the aggregate report records the gate as failed and the runner exits non-zero
